info.bio:
Los Tokens son un grupo vocal americano de doo-wop de Brooklyn, Nueva York.  Conocidos, sobre todo, por su disco, "The Lion Sleeps Tonight" de 1961.

 El grupo se formó en 1955 en Brooklyn, en la Abraham Lincoln High School, y conocido con el nombre de Linc-Tones. Inicialmente formado por Neil Sedaka, Hank Medress, Eddie Rabkin, y Cynthia Zolotin. Rabkin fue sustituido por Jay Siegel en 1956, y la banda grabó su primer single, "While I Dream" .

scenes.name: Antes del diluvio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «edad oscura» del rock'n'roll: los rebeldes son sustituidos por ídolos adolescentes educados y el Brill Building devuelve el poder a los compositores profesionales. Pero en esos años se incuban la revolución futura: la guitarra fuzz de Link Wray, los bailes de moda (el twist), el rock instrumental de guitarras (Duane Eddy, Ventures, Shadows), el calipso y el primer ska, el doo-wop más inventivo (Coasters, Drifters, Five Royales), el nacimiento del soul (Sam Cooke, Ray Charles, Motown, Stax), el estudio como instrumento de Joe Meek y el surf de los Beach Boys y del «muro de sonido» de Phil Spector.

podcast.body: Today, there are two touring versions of The Tokens, one led by Jay Siegel and another by Phil Margo. "Today there are two touring versions of The Tokens, one led by J C Eagle and one by Phil Margo."

podcast.title: Early Lineup with Neil Sedaka
podcast.body: The group was originally known as The Linktones and was led by Neil Sedaka, who sang lead vocals on their song "Will I Dream." "They were the group, also known as the Linktones, that was led by Carol King's friend Neil Sadaka, and who'd recorded Will I Dream with Sadaka Unlead Focals."

podcast.title: First Vocal Group to Produce a Hit for Another Vocal Group
podcast.body: The Tokens transitioned into record production themselves, achieving greater success than as performers. They produced records like The Chiffons' "He's So Fine," making them the first vocal group to produce a hit for another vocal group. "There they were far more successful, and as a group they produced records like the Schiffons, he's so fine, making them the first vocal group to produce a hit for another vocal group."

podcast.title: Group Splits and Sedaka's Solo Career
podcast.body: After an early member went to college and was replaced by Jay Siegel, the group split up. Neil Sedaka then embarked on a very successful career as a solo performer and songwriter. "But then the group had split up, and Sadaka had gone on to a very successful career as a solo performer and a songwriter."

podcast.title: Initial Flops on RCA
podcast.body: The Tokens released a couple of flop singles on RCA, including a remake of "The Moon Glows," before recording "The Lion Sleeps Tonight." "The group put out a couple of flop singles on RCA, including a remake of the Moon Glows"

podcast.title: Jay Siegel and Hank Medress Form Darryl and the Oxfords
podcast.body: Following the initial split of The Tokens, Jay Siegel and Hank Medress continued performing together and formed a new group called Darryl and the Oxfords with two other singers. "But Siegel and one of the other group members, Hank Madress, had carried on performing together, and had formed a new group, Darryl and the Oxfords with two other singers."

podcast.title: Record Deal for Neil Sedaka's Group
podcast.body: After Neil Sedaka co-wrote "While I Dream" and sang it with his group, The Linktones, the group secured a record deal under the name The Tokens. This achievement inspired Carole King to pursue songwriting. "Siddak had briefly dated her and had co-written that song himself with Howard Greenfield, and his group got a record deal under the name The Tokens."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Reforming as The Tokens with Margo Brothers
podcast.body: After Darryl and the Oxfords also split, Siegel and Medress invited Mitch Margot and his 12-year-old brother Phil to join them. This new lineup revived the old name of The Tokens. "But that group had also split up, so the duo invited yet another pair of singers to join them, Mitch Margot, who was around their age in his late teens, and his 12-year-old brother Phil."

podcast.title: Working with Hugo and Luigi
podcast.body: After their first hit on Warwick Records, the group signed to RCA Records and began working with the production duo Hugo and Luigi, known for their work on "Shout." "But by then, the group had signed to RCA Records, and were now working with Hugo and the Ouija, the production duo, who you might remember from the episode on Shout."
